content.title: How to watch and listen to Seattle Mariners games in 2026 on TV, streaming, and radio
content.text: SEATTLE — The Seattle Mariners have high hopes to compete for a World Series title in 2026 after a heartbreaking end to last season.For fans unable to attend in person, Mariners games will be more accessible than ever.RELATED | The complete 2026 guide to Seattle Mariners Games at T-Mobile ParkMariners TV will replace ROOT Sports, which shut down after the 2025 baseball season. Major League Baseball is taking over the producing and distributing of all local games in 2026.Aaron Goldsmith is returning as the lead television announcer in his 14th season with the Mariners. Rick Rizzs will lead the radio side in his final year alongside Gary Hill Jr.250 truckloads of food delivered to all 50 states for America250Angie Mentink, Jay Buhner, Ryan Rowland-Smith, Dave Valle, and Brad Adam will all return as announcers.StreamingFans will be able to stream games on Mariners.tv for $99.99 for the whole season or $19.99 per month.Diehard baseball fans can bundle Mariners.tv with MLB.tv to see all games from around the league. That package is $199.99 for the season or $39.99 monthly.All packages include a seven-day free trial for fans who want to test out the service first.Mariners.tv is available to residents of Washington, Idaho, Oregon, Alaska, Montana, and Hawaii.Mariners fans outside of those states will be able to access games through the usual MLB.tv.Fans within the Mariners' regional viewing area have historically been blacked out of games through MLB.tv to avoid conflicts with local television providers.Nationally broadcast games may not be available on Mariners.tv; viewers will need to tune into the specific channel for that game.TelevisionMariners games will also continue to be available through traditional cable and satellite avenues.The full channel finder is available here. Fans can enter a zip code and find the available channel.Xfinity/ComcastChannel 1261DirecTVChannel 687Spectrum/CharterBillings - Channel 130Bozeman - Channel 130Butte - Channel 130Eugene - Channel 414Great Falls - Channel 130Helena - Channel 130Kennewick - Channel 414Klamath Falls - Channel 414Medford - Channel 414Missoula - Channel 130Portland - Channel 414Seattle - Channel 414Spokane - Channel 318 or 414Tacoma - Channel 414Yakima - Channel 414Astound/WaveBellingham - Channel 26 and 126Camano Island - Channel 46 and 246Chelan - Channel 31 and 131Depoe Bay - Channel 31 and 737Duvall - Channel 37 and 737Echo Lake - Channel 31 and 737Entiat - Channel 31 and 737Lewis County - Channel 41 and 541Port Angeles - Channel 25 and 125Port Orchard - Channel 30 and 130Port Townsend - Channel 33 and 733Salem - Channel 38 and 738Sandy - Channel 43 and 738Seattle - Channel 37 and 737Sheridan - Channel 38 and 738Silverton - Channel 38 and 738Stayton - Channel 38 and 738Stevenson - Channel 57 and 157Whidbey Island - Channel 31 and 737TDSBend - Channel 27 and 627Coeur d'Alene - Channel 276 and 1276Lapine - Channel 27 and 627Madras - Channel 32 and 132Prineville - Channel 32 and 132TDSTV+ - Channel 243FuboAvailable channelProviders without Mariners TVClick!NetworkDISH NetworkElauwit NetworksHulu + Live TVPhiloPluto TVSling TVYouTube TVOther providers not listed with specific channelsMany Mariners fans who watch games through their TV have been frustrated with the announcement so close to the season opener.Unlike Root Sports' channel, the new Mariners TV channel will only be on the air for games—including pregame and postgame coverage.Nationally broadcast games may not be available on the Mariners TV channel; viewers will need to tune into the specific channel for that game.RadioFans can listen to all Mariners games on 710 AM on the radio."Catch all Mariners games on the flagship station and its affiliates in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Alaska, and British Columbia," the team said on its website.Radio broadcasts can also be heard on MLB.tv for subscribers and the Seattle Sports app.Rick Rizzs, the iconic Mariners broadcaster, will retire at the conclusion of the 2026 season.RELATED | There will never be another Rick RizzsRizzs' retirement ends a vibrant career of more than 40 years as the voice of the Seattle Mariners.The 72-year-old was originally hired in 1983 to pair with Ford C. Frick Award-winning broadcaster Dave Niehaus, a well-known and Rizzs' cherished friend who died in 2010.Outside of a three-year stint with the Tigers from 1992-1994, Rizzs cemented himself as the longest-tenured broadcaster in Mariners history.
